top_choice_rationale: P001 (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) credits induced proximity to the ubiquitin-proteasome system as a new chemical design principle: catalytic, event-driven destruction of targets that lack conventional binding pockets. It is reproduced across academic and industrial laboratories, quantitatively characterised through ternary-complex cooperativity, and clinically validated through cereblon-based glue drugs. Handa's cereblon mechanism ties the glue strand to the degrader concept, so one citation covers both honestly, though credit for Sakamoto, Ciulli, Gray, Ito and Kim is left out by the three-name cap and heterobifunctional degrader approval remains unconfirmed. P003 follows as the most mature molecular-design achievement, P002 as a complete but more incremental method, and P004 last among awards because in-cell evidence is still contested.
